info.title: Arcus WebSocket API
info.description:
Real-time WebSocket API for Arcus. Provides live market data streams and account update subscriptions over a single persistent connection.

## Connection

Connect to the WebSocket endpoint. All channels share one connection — there is no per-channel handshake.

## Protocol

All messages are JSON. Four top-level `type` values exist:

| `type`        | Direction       | Purpose |
|---------------|-----------------|---------|
| `subscribe`   | client → server | Start receiving a channel |
| `unsubscribe` | client → server | Stop receiving a channel |
| `post`        | client → server | Order mutation (placeOrder, cancelOrder, modifyOrder) |
| `get`         | client → server | Read-only RPC snapshot |
| `subscribed`  | server → client | Subscribe ack + initial snapshot |
| `unsubscribed`| server → client | Unsubscribe ack |
| `channel_data`| server → client | Real-time update |
| `degraded`    | server → client | Initial snapshot withheld; subscribe pending server-side retry |

## Degraded subscriptions

When the initial snapshot for a subscribe cannot be served, the server keeps the subscription pending — it never delivers a wrong or gappy snapshot — and sends a single notice:

```json
{"type":"degraded","channel":"orders","id":"0x…","accountIndex":0,"reason":"snapshot_unavailable","retryAfterMs":5000}
```

| `reason`               | Meaning |
|------------------------|---------|
| `snapshot_stale`       | Persistence snapshot too far behind the live stream to join it without a gap |
| `snapshot_unavailable` | Snapshot backend read failed |

The server retries the snapshot (roughly every `retryAfterMs`, advisory) and completes the subscribe with a normal `subscribed` frame once it can be served — no client action is required. `id` is omitted on global channels. Clients should surface a stale/degraded indicator until the `subscribed` frame arrives.

## Signing

Two signing schemes are used depending on the method.

### Typed canonical payload (placeOrder / cancelOrder / modifyOrder and batch variants)

The payload JSON object IS the signing message — there is no separate prefix. Keys are emitted in fixed alphabetical order; values are engine-native integers (ticks, quantums, enums), not decimal strings. Ed25519 sign the UTF-8 bytes of this string directly.

```
placeOrder / batchPlaceOrders element  (op=1; op=4 for TPSL legs):
  {"ad":"0x…","ai":N,[,"c":"…"],"ct":N,"g":N,"m":N,"op":1,"p":N,"q":N,"r":0|1,"s":N,"t":N,"v":1}

cancelOrder / batchCancelOrders element:
  {"ad":"0x…","ai":N,[,"c":"…"],"ct":N,[,"id":"…"],"m":N,"op":2,"v":1}

modifyOrder / batchModifyOrders element (exactly one of id / c):
  {"ad":"0x…","ai":N,[,"c":"…"],"ct":N,"g":N,[,"id":"…"],"m":N,"op":3,"p":N,"q":N,"r":0|1,"s":N,"t":N,"v":1}
```

`ct` is the client timestamp in nanoseconds — the same value as `timestamp` on the request envelope (and the `X-Timestamp` header on REST). Generate it once per request with `time.now_ns()` / `Date.now() * 1_000_000` and use it in both places. The server rejects values outside ±30 s of its wall-clock.

Include `apiKey`, `timestamp`, and `signature` on the `request` object. The `apiKey` is your Ed25519 public key (64 hex characters).

**Batch methods are signed per element.** `batchPlaceOrders`, `batchCancelOrders`, and `batchModifyOrders` do NOT carry a single `request.signature`. Each element of `payload.orders` / `payload.cancels` / `payload.modifies` carries its own `signature` over the typed canonical payload for that element — byte-for-byte identical to the signature a standalone order would carry — and the `request` envelope carries only the shared `apiKey` + `timestamp`.

### Legacy scheme (cancelAllOrders / setLeverage / adjustIsolatedMargin)

```
timestamp_ns + action + canonicalJSON(request.payload)
```

where `action` is the canonical camelCase method name (e.g. `cancelAllOrders`) and `timestamp_ns` is the nanosecond epoch string that also appears on the request envelope.

l2Orderbook.description:
> **Endpoint:** `wss://api.arcus.xyz/v1/ws` — one socket multiplexes every channel and RPC request. Click **Connect**, then send the example subscribe message below to start receiving data.

Periodic full L2 orderbook snapshots for a single market. On subscribe, the server sends the current book up to `nLevels` price levels per side, then continues to broadcast a fresh full snapshot every ~200ms.

No incremental updates — each message replaces the prior book state. Use `l2OrderbookUpdates` if you need to maintain your own local book.

A connection may subscribe more than once to the same market when each subscribe uses a distinct (`sigFigs`, `roundStep`) pair. `subscribed`, `channel_data`, and `unsubscribed` frames echo those fields (omitted for full precision) so the client can demux views. Unsubscribe must include the same pair to drop one view without affecting the others.

l2OrderbookUpdates.description:
> **Endpoint:** `wss://api.arcus.xyz/v1/ws` — one socket multiplexes every channel and RPC request. Click **Connect**, then send the example subscribe message below to start receiving data.

Full L2 orderbook snapshot followed by event-driven incremental deltas for a single market.

On subscribe: full snapshot up to `nLevels` per side, then delta updates as orders are placed, modified, or cancelled. Each delta carries a monotonically increasing per-market `lastSequenceId`.

Reconciliation (splice rule): the snapshot is a periodic generation that lags slightly behind the live delta head, so the first delta after the snapshot may be a few sequences ahead of the snapshot's `lastSequenceId` — this small boundary gap is expected and self-heals. Seed from the snapshot, then apply every delta whose `lastSequenceId` exceeds the snapshot's; do NOT require the first delta to equal `snapshotSeq + 1`, and do NOT drop or re-subscribe on the initial boundary gap. Once you are applying deltas, sequences are contiguous; a gap that appears mid-stream indicates a genuine problem — resubscribe then. A single delta frame may list the same price more than once; apply entries in array order, last-write-wins per price.

trades.description:
> **Endpoint:** `wss://api.arcus.xyz/v1/ws` — one socket multiplexes every channel and RPC request. Click **Connect**, then send the example subscribe message below to start receiving data.

Public trade stream for a single market. No snapshot on subscribe — only live updates from the moment of subscription.

Each message is an array of fills from a single taker order match. All fills in one array share the same `takerOrderId`, `takerAccountId`, `timestamp`, and `sequenceNumber`.

markets.description:
> **Endpoint:** `wss://api.arcus.xyz/v1/ws` — one socket multiplexes every channel and RPC request. Click **Connect**, then send the example subscribe message below to start receiving data.

Global channel — no `id` required. Streams full per-market metadata for all listed markets.

Snapshot-only channel: every message is a full map of all markets keyed by `marketId` (same shape on subscribe and on every periodic re-emission, no partial diffs). Clients replace their entire markets view on each message.

**Cadence:** ~5s periodic snapshot, plus an immediate snapshot when a new funding rate is applied (~hourly) so the just-applied `fundingRate` propagates without waiting for the next periodic snapshot.

**Field coverage today:** `marketDisplayName`, `marketId`, `baseAsset`, `quoteAsset`, `status` (currently always `ONLINE`), static config (tick/step/min/max sizes, margin fractions, fees), `oraclePrice`, `fundingRate`, `nextFundingRate`, and `nextFundingAt` are populated. `priceChange24h` is the fractional change in the **mark price** over the trailing 24h (not the oracle price). `volume24h`, `high24h`, `low24h`, and `trades24h` are rolling 24h aggregates, refreshed periodically. High/low use only closed candles with at least one trade (gap-fill buckets are excluded). `openInterest` is the total size of all open long positions per market (equals total short), in base asset units, refreshed from a periodic snapshot (default ~60s) so it may lag real time. `openInterestCapNotional` (`null` when no cap is active) is the operator-set maximum open-interest USD notional, refreshed on the same cadence.

oraclePrices.description:
> **Endpoint:** `wss://api.arcus.xyz/v1/ws` — one socket multiplexes every channel and RPC request. Click **Connect**, then send the example subscribe message below to start receiving data.

Per-market oracle price updates sourced from the on-chain slinky aggregator. Pushes a new price on each oracle update.

bbo.description:
> **Endpoint:** `wss://api.arcus.xyz/v1/ws` — one socket multiplexes every channel and RPC request. Click **Connect**, then send the example subscribe message below to start receiving data.

Best bid and offer (top-of-book) for a single market. Lower bandwidth than `l2Orderbook` when only the inside quote is needed.

account.description:
> **Endpoint:** `wss://api.arcus.xyz/v1/ws` — one socket multiplexes every channel and RPC request. Click **Connect**, then send the example subscribe message below to start receiving data.

Account state snapshot and streaming updates for a single sub-account.

**No authentication required at subscribe time** — pass the account's Ethereum address as `id`. Snapshot on subscribe includes open positions, balances, and margin info. Periodic re-snapshots are sent every 5 seconds.

Update `type` values: `PLACED`, `CANCELED`, `MARGIN_CANCELED`, `REJECTED`, `TPSL_PLACED`, `TPSL_CANCELED`, `TPSL_TRIGGERED`, `LIQUIDATION`, `ADL`.

`FILL` events are routed to the `userFills` channel only and do not appear here. `LIQUIDATION` and `ADL` are fanned out to both `account` and `userFills`.

positions.description:
> **Endpoint:** `wss://api.arcus.xyz/v1/ws` — one socket multiplexes every channel and RPC request. Click **Connect**, then send the example subscribe message below to start receiving data.

Open positions for a single sub-account. Snapshot contents use `PositionsSnapshot`: the REST `GET /positions` positions map plus `isSnapshot: true`, `lastSequenceId`, `address`, and `accountIndex`. Updates carry one `PositionUpdate` event per frame.

`cumulativeFunding` is absent from streaming events — use the snapshot for funding horizons. On close (size drops to 0), the row is emitted in `FLAT` form with zeroed financials.

`leverage` reflects the user's per-(account, market) override (set via REST `POST /v1/setLeverage`) when present, otherwise the market default. A `PositionUpdate` is also emitted when the user adjusts leverage on a market they already hold a position in, and when they add or remove isolated margin via `POST /v1/adjustIsolatedMargin` (that frame carries `requestId` so clients can correlate it with the 202 ACK, and `marginMode: ISOLATED`).

Every perp position row — snapshot and streaming — includes `marginMode` (`CROSS` or `ISOLATED`) so clients can tell the collateral mode without a REST round-trip. Isolated rows set `marginUsed` to the posted isolated-leg pool (not IMR at mark); the full isolated-leg cash balance is derivable as `marginUsed + borrowedCapital`.

Optionally scoped to one market: pass `market` on subscribe (ticker or numeric id) and the snapshot, the live frames, and the post-snapshot catch-up all carry only that market. The filter is part of subscription identity, so one connection can hold several market-scoped views of the same account; `unsubscribe` must repeat the same `market`.

userFills.description:
> **Endpoint:** `wss://api.arcus.xyz/v1/ws` — one socket multiplexes every channel and RPC request. Click **Connect**, then send the example subscribe message below to start receiving data.

Per-user fill stream. Snapshot on subscribe contains recent fills; streaming updates deliver each new fill as orders are matched. Snapshot is sent once on connect only.

`LIQUIDATION` and `ADL` fills also appear here carrying the `liquidation` marker (`method` + `liquidatedUser`) — on the liquidated account's leg for `LIQUIDATION` and the deleveraged counterparty's leg for `ADL` — so subscribers tracking realized closures can observe forced fills on either `account` or `userFills`. The marker is persisted, so it is present in snapshots as well as live updates.

Optionally scoped to one market: pass `market` on subscribe (ticker or numeric id) and the snapshot, the live frames, and the post-snapshot catch-up all carry only that market. The filter is part of subscription identity, so one connection can hold several market-scoped views of the same account; `unsubscribe` must repeat the same `market`.

orders.description:
> **Endpoint:** `wss://api.arcus.xyz/v1/ws` — one socket multiplexes every channel and RPC request. Click **Connect**, then send the example subscribe message below to start receiving data.

Open and recently closed order updates for an account. Snapshot on subscribe includes all open orders and up to 100 recently closed orders. Streaming updates use a unified shape for both status changes and fill events. Snapshot is sent once on connect only.

Subscribe to this channel alongside `userFills` to observe the full order lifecycle after placing an order via the `orderOperations` channel.

Optionally scoped to one market: pass `market` on subscribe (ticker or numeric id) and the snapshot, the live frames, and the post-snapshot catch-up all carry only that market. The filter is part of subscription identity, so one connection can hold several market-scoped views of the same account; `unsubscribe` must repeat the same `market`.

funding.description:
> **Endpoint:** `wss://api.arcus.xyz/v1/ws` — one socket multiplexes every channel and RPC request. Click **Connect**, then send the example subscribe message below to start receiving data.

Funding payment stream for an account. Snapshot on subscribe contains up to 100 most recent funding payments from the last 30 days; for older history query REST `GET /v1/funding` with an explicit `from`. Live updates deliver one event per (market, account) at each funding payment time.

Sign convention on `payment`: positive = received, negative = paid. `time` is the Unix-microsecond funding payment time.

predictedFunding.description:
> **Endpoint:** `wss://api.arcus.xyz/v1/ws` — one socket multiplexes every channel and RPC request. Click **Connect**, then send the example subscribe message below to start receiving data.

Predicted next-hour funding rate for a single market. Subscribe `id` is the market display name (e.g. `BTC-USD`).

On subscribe the initial response carries the latest cached prediction for the market; `contents` is empty when no prediction has been published yet. Streaming updates deliver a new `{market, rate1h}` payload each time the funder recomputes the prediction. Unlike most channels, payloads are not wrapped in an `isSnapshot` envelope.

accountTransferUpdates.description:
> **Endpoint:** `wss://api.arcus.xyz/v1/ws` — one socket multiplexes every channel and RPC request. Click **Connect**, then send the example subscribe message below to start receiving data.

Account transfer events (deposits, withdrawals, transfers, referral claims) for an account. Snapshot on subscribe contains the most recent events newest-first (`isSnapshot: true`); each streaming update carries a single event (`isSnapshot: false`) as it is applied by the engine.

Amounts and balances are human-readable decimal strings in quote currency. `globalSequenceId` gives strict ordering across all engine events. The equivalent REST read is `GET /v1/accountTransferUpdates`.

accountAttributeUpdates.description:
> **Endpoint:** `wss://api.arcus.xyz/v1/ws` — one socket multiplexes every channel and RPC request. Click **Connect**, then send the example subscribe message below to start receiving data.

Per-account attribute state, discriminated by entry `type`. `type: "leverage"` entries carry effective leverage and margin mode per market. `isolated` and `marginMode` are always present — in the snapshot they reflect the current persisted state; in streaming frames they reflect the account's margin mode after the triggering event, defaulting to CROSS if the margin mode lookup fails. `type: "feeTier"` entries carry account-level fee tier state. `type: "leverageReject"` entries (streaming only) report that a setLeverage request was refused by the engine — this is the `REJECTED` half of the setLeverage lifecycle; an applied change arrives as a `leverage` entry. When `isolated` was also supplied on the request, both the leverage and margin mode outcomes are folded into the same entry via the optional `marginModeStatus` and `marginModeRejectReason` fields. Snapshot returns one leverage entry per market (carrying both leverage and margin mode state) plus, when available, one fee tier entry. Streaming delivers one entry for each changed attribute.

exchangeAttributeUpdates.description:
> **Endpoint:** `wss://api.arcus.xyz/v1/ws` — one socket multiplexes every channel and RPC request. Click **Connect**, then send the example subscribe message below to start receiving data.

Exchange-wide attribute state, discriminated by entry `type`:

`"feeTierConfig"` carries the full fee tier table whenever the fee tier table is updated.

`"marketAttributes"` (DEPRECATED — superseded by the dedicated `marketAttributes` channel, whose entries carry the market's full attribute state; this variant keeps streaming for existing consumers and will be removed after a deprecation window) carries per-market Regular Trading Hours and off-hours trading-bound events: RTH boundary crossings (`isOutsideRth`, with `boundEvent`: `exitRth` / `enterRth`), VWAP settlement seals (`sealedVwapSettlementPrice`), and off-hours expansion-zone events (`boundEvent`: `expansionZoneEntered` when a side's impact-price EWMA crosses within 90% of its trading boundary, starting the 1-hour expansion clock; `expansionZoneExited` when the EWMA relaxes out of the zone and the clock resets; `tradingBoundExpanded` when the clock completes and that side's band widens one level on the 0.5×→1×→2×→4× ladder).

**Global channel — no `id` required.** All subscribers receive the same stream.

On subscribe: snapshot of the current fee tier table (one `feeTierConfig` entry, `isSnapshot: true`). Streaming: fee tier table replacements and marketAttributes edge events (`isSnapshot: false`).

The equivalent REST reads are `GET /v1/feetiers` and `GET /v1/markets` (`isOutsideRth`, `isUpperInExpansionZone` / `isLowerInExpansionZone`, `upperTradingBound` / `lowerTradingBound`).

marketAttributes.description:
> **Endpoint:** `wss://api.arcus.xyz/v1/ws` — one socket multiplexes every channel and RPC request. Click **Connect**, then send the example subscribe message below to start receiving data.

Per-market Regular Trading Hours / off-hours attribute state for every online market. 24/7 markets (crypto) are included with `isOutsideRth: false` — they never leave regular trading hours — and every other off-hours field `null`; they never produce streaming updates. Supersedes the `marketAttributes` entry variant on `exchangeAttributeUpdates`.

Every entry — snapshot and streaming alike — is the market's COMPLETE current attribute block: `marketId`, `marketDisplayName`, `offHoursInitialMarginFraction`, `isOutsideRth`, `currentSettlementPrice`, both trading-band boundaries and next-level boundaries, and per-side expansion-zone state. Fields that do not currently apply are `null`, never omitted. Field semantics match `GET /v1/markets`.

**Global channel — no `id` required.** All subscribers receive the same stream.

On subscribe: one full block per online market (`isSnapshot: true`) — a complete bootstrap, no REST read needed. Streaming: a single-entry envelope with the affected market's full post-event block on every RTH boundary crossing, VWAP seal, and off-hours bound event (`isSnapshot: false`). Because each update carries the full block — both sides' bounds, not just the side an event fired on — clients replace their local entry for `marketId` wholesale; `boundEvent` annotates what fired — always present on delta entries (`exitRth` / `enterRth` on RTH boundary crossings, a bound-event name otherwise); `boundSide` is also always present on delta entries (null on RTH-transition / non-bound-event deltas).

candles.description:
> **Endpoint:** `wss://api.arcus.xyz/v1/ws` — one socket multiplexes every channel and RPC request. Click **Connect**, then send the example subscribe message below to start receiving data.

OHLCV candlestick stream. Subscribe `id` is `"MARKET/TIMEFRAME"`, e.g. `"BTC-USD/1m"`.

On subscribe: snapshot of the most recent candles (up to 200). Then: real-time updates as each bar changes. Open-candle updates are coalesced and sent at most about every 250 ms per market/timeframe. `isFinal: true` updates are sent immediately when the interval closes and the bar will not be updated again.

Available timeframes: `1m`, `3m`, `5m`, `15m`, `30m`, `1h`, `2h`, `4h`, `8h`, `12h`, `1d`, `3d`, `1w`.

orderOperations.description:
> **Endpoint:** `wss://api.arcus.xyz/v1/ws` — one socket multiplexes every channel and RPC request. Click **Connect**, then send the example subscribe message below to start receiving data.

RPC-style trading operations over WebSocket. Use `type: post` for order mutations and `type: get` for read-only snapshots.

Every request carries a client-chosen numeric `id` that is echoed in the response, allowing you to correlate replies with requests. Use a monotonically increasing counter per connection.

**Order mutations are asynchronous** — they reply with `status: 202` (accepted, not terminal). Subscribe to `orders` and `userFills` to observe the full order lifecycle.

**Supported `post` methods:** `placeOrder`, `cancelOrder`, `cancelAllOrders`, `scheduleCancel`, `modifyOrder`, `batchPlaceOrders`, `batchCancelOrders`, `batchModifyOrders`, `setLeverage`, `adjustIsolatedMargin`.

**Supported `get` methods:** `l2orderbook`, `bbo`, `mids`, `account`, `fills`, `orders`, `markets`, `prices`, `positions`, `leverages`, `ratelimit`.

examples.name: BTC-USD snapshot aggregated to 3 sig figs

L2OrderbookUpdate.name: L2OrderbookUpdate
L2OrderbookUpdate.title: L2 Orderbook Incremental Update
L2OrderbookUpdate.description: `size: "0"` means the level was removed. Apply every delta whose `lastSequenceId` exceeds the snapshot's; the first delta may be a few sequences ahead of the snapshot (an expected boundary gap that self-heals — do **not** re-subscribe on it). Once you are applying deltas, sequences are contiguous, so only a **mid-stream** gap means a missed delta — re-subscribe for a fresh snapshot then.

MarketsSnapshot.name: MarketsSnapshot
MarketsSnapshot.title: Markets Snapshot
MarketsSnapshot.description: Full markets state delivered as the subscribe response. Same shape as the periodic `MarketsUpdate` — the markets channel is snapshot-only.

MarketsUpdate.name: MarketsUpdate
MarketsUpdate.title: Markets Update
MarketsUpdate.description: Periodic re-snapshot of all markets. Replaces the client's full markets view; there are no partial diffs on this channel.

AccountSnapshot.name: AccountSnapshot
AccountSnapshot.title: Account Snapshot
AccountSnapshot.description: Full account state sent on subscribe, re-broadcast every 5 seconds, and sent shortly after account events. Schema: openapi `AccountsSnapshot` — not the REST `GET /account` shape (`lastSequenceId` and `accountEquity` instead of `sequenceNumber` and `equity`).

AccountUpdate.name: AccountUpdate
AccountUpdate.title: Account Update
AccountUpdate.description: Streaming account event. `type` in `contents` is one of: `PLACED`, `CANCELED`, `MARGIN_CANCELED`, `REJECTED`, `TPSL_PLACED`, `TPSL_CANCELED`, `TPSL_TRIGGERED`, `LIQUIDATION`, `ADL`. `netQuoteBalance` is stamped on every frame. `avgFillPrice` is present whenever the order has any filled quantity (e.g. a cancel after partial fills) and matches the REST / snapshot value.

PositionsSnapshot.name: PositionsSnapshot
PositionsSnapshot.title: Positions Snapshot
PositionsSnapshot.description: Sent once on subscribe. Contents use OpenAPI `PositionsSnapshot`: the same `positions` map as REST `GET /positions` (`GetPositionsResponse`) plus required `isSnapshot: true`, `lastSequenceId`, `address`, and `accountIndex`. The snapshot does NOT carry the REST-only `total` field. The required `positions` map is keyed by perp market id; each row carries `sequenceNumber`.

PositionUpdate.name: PositionUpdate
PositionUpdate.title: Position Update
PositionUpdate.description:
One position delta per frame (one `PositionUpdate` per streaming event). Contents carry `isSnapshot: false` and `lastSequenceId`. Each update has one row in `positions`.

Each perp position row carries `sequenceNumber` (same counter as AccountUpdate). `cumulativeFunding` is absent; use the snapshot for funding horizons. On close, emitted in `FLAT` form with zeroed financials.

AccountAttributesSnapshot.name: AccountAttributesSnapshot
AccountAttributesSnapshot.title: Account Attributes Snapshot
AccountAttributesSnapshot.description: One leverage entry per market (carrying both leverage and margin mode state), plus one fee tier entry when available. Sent once on subscribe.

AccountAttributesUpdate.name: AccountAttributesUpdate
AccountAttributesUpdate.title: Account Attributes Update
AccountAttributesUpdate.description: Single-entry delta keyed by `type`. A `leverage` or `feeTier` entry is a state change; a `leverageReject` entry reports a refused request (no state change). When `isolated` was part of a `setLeverage` request the margin mode outcome is carried inside the same entry.

ExchangeAttributesSnapshot.name: ExchangeAttributesSnapshot
ExchangeAttributesSnapshot.title: Exchange Attributes Snapshot
ExchangeAttributesSnapshot.description: Initial snapshot sent once on subscribe. Contains one `feeTierConfig` entry with the complete current fee tier table (`isSnapshot: true`).

ExchangeAttributesUpdate.name: ExchangeAttributesUpdate
ExchangeAttributesUpdate.title: Exchange Attributes Update
ExchangeAttributesUpdate.description: Streaming update pushed whenever an operator edits the exchange fee tier config. Always carries the full updated table in a single `feeTierConfig` entry (`isSnapshot: false`). Clients should replace their local copy atomically.

MarketAttributesSnapshot.name: MarketAttributesSnapshot
MarketAttributesSnapshot.title: Market Attributes Snapshot
MarketAttributesSnapshot.description: Initial snapshot sent once on subscribe: one complete attribute block per online market, 24/7 crypto included (`isSnapshot: true`). Every field is present on every entry — `null` when it does not currently apply — so no REST bootstrap is needed.

examples.name: Snapshot with a 24/7, an off-hours, and an in-RTH market

MarketAttributesStreamUpdate.name: MarketAttributesStreamUpdate
MarketAttributesStreamUpdate.title: Market Attributes Update
MarketAttributesStreamUpdate.description: Streaming update pushed on every RTH boundary crossing, VWAP seal, and off-hours bound event. The single entry is the affected market's full post-event attribute block — both sides' bounds, not just the side an event fired on — so clients replace their local entry for `marketId` wholesale. `boundEvent` annotates what fired — always present on delta entries (`exitRth` / `enterRth` on RTH boundary crossings, a bound-event name otherwise); `boundSide` is also always present on delta entries (null on RTH-transition / non-bound-event deltas).

UserFillsSnapshot.name: UserFillsSnapshot
UserFillsSnapshot.title: User Fills Snapshot
UserFillsSnapshot.description: Recent fills sent once on subscribe.

UserFillUpdate.name: UserFillUpdate
UserFillUpdate.title: User Fill Update
UserFillUpdate.description: One fill per frame as orders are matched.

OrdersSnapshot.name: OrdersSnapshot
OrdersSnapshot.title: Orders Snapshot
OrdersSnapshot.description: Open orders plus recently closed orders with `isSnapshot: true` and `lastSequenceId` (per-account sequence at snapshot time). Sent once on subscribe.

OrderUpdate.name: OrderUpdate
OrderUpdate.title: Order Update
OrderUpdate.description: One order lifecycle event. Carries `sequenceNumber` (per-account, same counter as AccountUpdate).

FundingPaymentsSnapshot.name: FundingPaymentsSnapshot
FundingPaymentsSnapshot.title: Funding Payments Snapshot
FundingPaymentsSnapshot.description: Recent funding payments for the account, sent once on subscribe. Same item shape as REST `GET /v1/funding`. Up to 100 entries from the last 30 days; for older history query REST `GET /v1/funding` with `from`.

FundingPaymentUpdate.name: FundingPaymentUpdate
FundingPaymentUpdate.title: Funding Payment Update
FundingPaymentUpdate.description: One applied funding payment per frame, emitted at each funding payment time. One frame per (market, account) where the position held a non-zero size when the payment was computed.

PredictedFundingSnapshot.name: PredictedFundingSnapshot
PredictedFundingSnapshot.title: Predicted Funding Snapshot
PredictedFundingSnapshot.description: Latest cached predicted rate for the market, sent once on subscribe. `contents` is empty when no prediction has been published yet.

PredictedFundingUpdate.name: PredictedFundingUpdate
PredictedFundingUpdate.title: Predicted Funding Update
PredictedFundingUpdate.description: New predicted next-hour funding rate, pushed each time the funder recomputes the prediction for the market.

AccountTransferUpdatesSnapshot.name: AccountTransferUpdatesSnapshot
AccountTransferUpdatesSnapshot.title: Account Transfer Updates Snapshot
AccountTransferUpdatesSnapshot.description: Recent account transfer events for the account, newest-first, sent once on subscribe (`isSnapshot: true`). `accountTransferEvents` is empty when the account has no recent events.

AccountTransferUpdateEvent.name: AccountTransferUpdateEvent
AccountTransferUpdateEvent.title: Account Transfer Update
AccountTransferUpdateEvent.description: A single applied transfer event (`isSnapshot: false`, one entry in `accountTransferEvents`), emitted as each deposit / withdrawal / transfer is applied by the engine.

CandleUpdate.name: CandleUpdate
CandleUpdate.title: Candle Update
CandleUpdate.description: A single candle bar update. Same shape as `Candle` in `openapi.yaml`. Open-candle updates are coalesced to at most about every 250 ms per market/timeframe. `isFinal: true` when the bar interval has closed; final updates are sent immediately.

SetLeverageRequest.name: SetLeverageRequest
SetLeverageRequest.title: Set Leverage
SetLeverageRequest.description: Per-`(account, market)` leverage. Mirrors `POST /v1/setLeverage`. `leverage` is an integer in `[1, market max]`; values outside this range are rejected with `400`. The WS path returns immediately on accept (envelope `status: 202`, body `status: ACK`); subscribe to the `accountAttributes` channel to observe the engine-confirmed outcome: an APPLIED change arrives as a `leverage` entry, a REJECTED one as a `leverageReject` entry (carrying the same `requestId` for correlation).

AdjustIsolatedMarginRequest.name: AdjustIsolatedMarginRequest
AdjustIsolatedMarginRequest.title: Adjust Isolated Margin
AdjustIsolatedMarginRequest.description: Move margin between the cross bucket and an isolated-mode position's leg for `(account, market)`. Mirrors `POST /v1/adjustIsolatedMargin`. `amount` is dollars as a decimal string (e.g. `"100"` for $100) — do not send quote quantums; the gateway converts dollars to quantums for the engine. Positive adds to the leg (cross → isolated), negative removes from the leg (isolated → cross), zero is rejected with `400`. The WS path returns immediately on accept (envelope `status: 202`, body `status: ACK`); the engine-confirmed post-state arrives on the `positions` channel as a `PositionUpdate` (correlated by `requestId`).

examples.name: Add 100 USDC of margin to BTC-USD isolated leg

CancelAllOrdersRequest.name: CancelAllOrdersRequest
CancelAllOrdersRequest.title: Cancel All Orders
CancelAllOrdersRequest.description: Cancels every open order for `(address, accountIndex)`. Pass `marketId` to scope the cancel to a single market; omit it to cancel across all markets. Untriggered TPSL orders in scope are canceled too. Mirrors `POST /v1/cancelAllOrders`.

ScheduleCancelRequest.name: ScheduleCancelRequest
ScheduleCancelRequest.title: Schedule Cancel
ScheduleCancelRequest.description:
Dead man's switch. Arm, refresh, or disarm a cancel-all deadline. Mirrors `POST /v1/scheduleCancel`.

Keep the switch armed by sending a **new** `time` (updated absolute epoch microseconds, 5s–5min ahead of now — typically `now + 60s`) before the current deadline. Reusing a past `time` does not extend the previous arm. Omit `time` (or send null) to disarm. If the deadline elapses without a refresh, the gateway fires `cancelAllOrders`.

Omit `marketId` for an account-wide switch (fires cancel-all across every market), or set it to scope the switch to a single market. A per-market switch is independent of the account-wide switch and of other per-market switches on the same subaccount, and `marketId` selects which switch a given arm/refresh/disarm targets.

A wallet may hold only a bounded number of switches armed at once (across all subaccounts and markets); arming a new switch beyond that limit is rejected. Refreshing an already-armed switch is always allowed.

BatchPlaceOrdersRequest.name: BatchPlaceOrdersRequest
BatchPlaceOrdersRequest.title: Batch Place Orders
BatchPlaceOrdersRequest.description: Places up to 100 orders in one request. All orders must share the same `address` / `accountIndex`. Signed PER ELEMENT using the typed canonical payload: each element of `orders` carries its own `signature` over the same typed `placeOrder` payload the element would carry if submitted standalone (op=1 for regular orders, op=4 for TPSL legs). The `request` envelope carries only the shared `apiKey` + `timestamp`; there is no outer `request.signature`. Mirrors `POST /v1/batchPlaceOrders`.

BatchCancelOrdersRequest.name: BatchCancelOrdersRequest
BatchCancelOrdersRequest.title: Batch Cancel Orders
BatchCancelOrdersRequest.description: Cancels up to 100 orders in one request. All cancels must share the same `address` / `accountIndex`. Signed PER ELEMENT using the typed canonical payload: each element of `cancels` carries its own `signature` over the same typed `cancelOrder` payload the element would carry if submitted standalone. The `request` envelope carries only the shared `apiKey` + `timestamp`; there is no outer `request.signature`. Mirrors `POST /v1/batchCancelOrders`.

BatchModifyOrdersRequest.name: BatchModifyOrdersRequest
BatchModifyOrdersRequest.title: Batch Modify Orders
BatchModifyOrdersRequest.description: Modifies up to 100 resting orders in one request. All modifies must share the same `address` / `accountIndex`. Signed PER ELEMENT using the typed canonical payload: each element of `modifies` carries its own `signature` over the same typed `modifyOrder` payload the element would carry if submitted standalone (op=3). The `request` envelope carries only the shared `apiKey` + `timestamp`; there is no outer `request.signature`. Failures are per element — an element that fails validation or signature verification surfaces as a `status: ERROR` row in the response while the rest of the batch proceeds. Mirrors `POST /v1/batchModifyOrders`.

RpcResponse.name: RpcResponse
RpcResponse.title: RPC Response
RpcResponse.description: Response to a `post` or `get` request. `id` is always echoed from the request. Order mutations reply with `status: 202` (accepted, not terminal). Other methods reply with `status: 200` on success.

nLevels.description: Price levels per side in snapshot. Range 1–100.

sigFigs.description: Aggregate price levels to this many significant figures. Omit for full precision. Bids round down / asks round up to the bucket boundary and merged sizes are summed; applied before nLevels truncation. A second subscribe on the same market is allowed when this (with roundStep) differs from every view already held.

roundStep.description: Refines the finest bucket into steps of 1, 2, or 5. Takes effect only when sigFigs is 5; ignored otherwise. Unsubscribe must echo the same value used to subscribe.

nLevels.description: Price levels per side in the initial snapshot. Range 1–100.

snapshot.description: When false, suppress the initial book snapshot on subscribe and stream only incremental delta updates. Defaults to true.

id.description: Master Ethereum address (0x-prefixed) or an encoded internal account id. When an encoded id is used it already carries its own subaccount index; supplying `accountIndex` as well is allowed only if the two agree. Whichever spelling is sent, every response frame echoes the lowercase master address.

accountIndex.description: Subaccount of the address in `id` to subscribe to. Honored on the account-scoped channels — `account`, `positions`, `orders`, `userFills`, `funding`, `accountTransferUpdates`, `accountAttributeUpdates`. Omit for subaccount 0, which is what every client written before this field existed gets. It is part of subscription identity: each subaccount is a separate subscription with its own snapshot and stream, so one connection may hold several, and `unsubscribe` must repeat the same `accountIndex` — omitting it drops only subaccount 0. Supplying it on a channel that is not account-scoped (e.g. `l2Orderbook`, `trades`, `markets`) is an error, NOT a silently ignored field, for the same reason `market` is: a client that believed its stream was scoped to one subaccount would mis-handle the rest. A value outside 0-9 is likewise an error rather than a clamp — an out-of-range subaccount can never carry traffic, so accepting one returns a permanently silent subscription.

snapshot.description: When false, suppress the initial state snapshot on subscribe and stream only live updates (e.g. userFills, orders). Defaults to true.

nFills.description: Optional userFills-only snapshot size (default 500, max 500). Honored only on the userFills channel; ignored elsewhere. Live channel_data frames are unaffected.

market.description: Restrict this subscription to a single market. Honored only on `positions`, `orders`, and `userFills` — the account-scoped channels whose every frame is about exactly one market. Supplying it on any other channel (e.g. `account`, `accountTransferUpdates`) is an error, NOT a silently ignored field: a client that believed its stream was scoped to one market would mishandle every other market's data. Accepts the display ticker ("BTC-USD", case-insensitive) or the numeric market id ("1"), the same spellings as the REST `?market=` query param. Omit for every market; an unresolvable value is an error rather than an unfiltered stream. The filter applies to the subscribe snapshot, the live `channel_data` frames, and the post-snapshot catch-up alike, so the baseline and the diffs always describe the same markets. It is part of subscription identity: one connection may hold several market-filtered views of the same channel + id, and `unsubscribe` must repeat the market it subscribed with (an `unsubscribe` with no `market` matches only the unfiltered view). The `subscribed` / `unsubscribed` acks echo the resolved ticker.

snapshot.description: When false, suppress the initial state snapshot on subscribe and stream only live updates. Defaults to true.
When false, suppress the initial per-market snapshot on subscribe and stream only live updates. Defaults to true.

id.description: Market and timeframe joined with "/". Available timeframes: `1m`, `3m`, `5m`, `15m`, `30m`, `1h`, `2h`, `4h`, `8h`, `12h`, `1d`, `3d`, `1w`.

snapshot.description: When false, suppress the initial candles snapshot on subscribe and stream only live updates. Defaults to true.

ChannelDataEnvelope.description: Common envelope for all server-pushed channel messages.

type.description: `subscribed` for the initial snapshot; `channel_data` for updates.

id.description: Channel id (market, or the lowercase master Ethereum address on account-scoped channels). Absent for global channels. Always lowercase for addresses regardless of the spelling used to subscribe, so compare it case-insensitively.

accountIndex.description: Subaccount this frame belongs to. Present on EVERY frame of an account-scoped channel — `subscribed`, `unsubscribed`, `degraded`, and `channel_data` alike — including when it is 0, so a frame names its subaccount outright and no client needs a "missing means 0" rule. Omitted on every other channel. This is what makes several subaccounts of one address demuxable on a single connection: `id` alone is the master address and is identical across all of them.

sigFigs.description: Echo of the l2Orderbook aggregation this frame belongs to. Omitted on full-precision views and on every other channel. Lets a client holding several aggregations of the same market demux snapshots.

roundStep.description: Echo of the l2Orderbook roundStep for this view. Omitted unless sigFigs is 5 and roundStep was 2 or 5.

market.description: Display ticker of the market this frame belongs to, always the resolved ticker even when the client subscribed by numeric id. Present only on `positions` / `orders` / `userFills`; omitted on every other channel. Its meaning differs slightly by frame type. On `subscribed` / `unsubscribed` it echoes the market filter the subscription was created with, and is omitted for an unfiltered subscription. On `channel_data` it is the market of the frame itself, so an UNFILTERED subscriber sees it too — those channels emit one frame per market, so every frame has one. This is what lets a client demux, exactly as `sigFigs` / `roundStep` do for l2Orderbook: a connection holding several market-filtered views of one account matches each frame to the right view by this field. Clients that hold a single unfiltered view can ignore it.

contents.description: Channel-specific payload. Schema varies by channel.

DegradedNotice.description: Sent once when the initial snapshot for a subscribe cannot be served (too stale to join the live stream, or the backend read failed). The subscription stays pending; the server retries and completes it with a normal `subscribed` frame once a snapshot can be served.

id.description: Channel id (market, or the lowercase master Ethereum address on account-scoped channels). Absent for global channels.

accountIndex.description: Subaccount whose subscribe is degraded. Present on account-scoped channels — including when it is 0 — and omitted on every other channel, exactly as on `channel_data`. Each subaccount is its own subscription, so one can be degraded while another on the same address is already serving; without this field a client could not tell which of its pending subscribes the notice refers to.

retryAfterMs.description: Advisory server-side retry cadence in milliseconds.

bids.description: Price levels, best bid first. Each entry is `[price, size]`.

asks.description: Price levels, best ask first. Each entry is `[price, size]`.

lastSequenceId.description: Per-market orderbook sequence of the last update reflected in this snapshot. Reconcile `l2OrderbookUpdates` deltas against this — apply deltas whose `lastSequenceId` exceeds it.

globalSequenceId.description: Cross-market monotonic sequence. Omitted when zero.

timestamp.description: Unix microseconds when the snapshot was taken. Omitted when zero.

contents.description: Incremental delta. Each `[price, size]` entry sets that level's absolute size; `size: "0"` means the level was removed. Apply every delta whose `lastSequenceId` exceeds the snapshot's; the first delta may be a few sequences ahead of the snapshot (an expected boundary gap that self-heals — do **not** re-subscribe on it). Once you are applying deltas, sequences are contiguous, so only a **mid-stream** gap means a missed delta — re-subscribe for a fresh snapshot then.

lastSequenceId.description: Per-market orderbook sequence for this delta. Monotonically increasing; the first delta after a snapshot may be a few sequences ahead of the snapshot's `lastSequenceId` (expected boundary gap). Apply any delta whose `lastSequenceId` exceeds the snapshot's; sequences are contiguous once you are applying deltas.

contents.description: Array of fills from one taker order match. All entries share `takerOrderId`, `takerAccountId`, `timestamp`, and `sequenceNumber`.

isSnapshot.description: Always `true` on this channel — every emission is a full snapshot, not a partial diff.

markets.description: All markets keyed by `marketId` as a string. Same per-market shape as REST `GET /v1/markets` (`MarketInfo`).

minOrderSize.description: Minimum order quantity, in base-asset units.

maxOrderSize.description: Maximum order quantity, in base-asset units. A per-order security gate rather than a dust filter — reduce-only orders are NOT exempt.

markPrice.description: Authoritative mark price (decimal string) — the sole risk-valuation price. "0" means unavailable; callers must not fall back to `oraclePrice`.

lastTradePrice.description: Price of the most recent trade (decimal string). Omitted until the market has traded.

nextFundingRate.description: In-progress forecast for the next funding payment.

nextFundingAt.description: Unix seconds for the next funding payment time.

priceChange24h.description: Fractional change in the mark price (not the oracle price) over the trailing 24h (e.g. "0.025" = +2.5%), computed from a rolling per-market ring of the first mark price seen each minute.

volume24h.description: Base-asset trade volume over the trailing 24h, from the rolling-24h aggregator.

high24h.description: Highest transaction price over the trailing 24h, from closed 1m candles with at least one trade.

low24h.description: Lowest transaction price over the trailing 24h, from closed 1m candles with at least one trade.

trades24h.description: Trade count over the trailing 24h, from the rolling-24h aggregator.

openInterest.description: Total size of all open long positions in the market (equals total short), in base asset units. Refreshed from a periodic snapshot, so it may lag real time.

openInterestCapNotional.description: Operator-set maximum open interest as a USD-notional decimal string (openInterest × mark price). At the cap the engine rejects OI-increasing fills with rejection reason OPEN_INTEREST_CAP_EXCEEDED; OI-neutral and OI-reducing trades still match. `null` when no cap is active. Refreshed from a periodic snapshot, so it may lag real time.

offHoursInitialMarginFraction.description: Initial margin fraction the engine enforces outside `regularTradingHours` (overnight/weekends for equity-class markets); equals `initialMarginFraction` for 24/7 markets. Maintenance margin is not uplifted off-hours.

currentSettlementPrice.description: Sealed VWAP settlement price (decimal USD) anchoring the off-hours trading band. Present only while outside RTH with a sealed anchor; omitted in-RTH and for 24/7 markets.

upperTradingBound.description: Actual upper price boundary (decimal USD) of the off-hours trading band the engine enforces (anchor + anchor × initialMarginFraction × bandMultiplier; the multiplier walks the 0.5×→1×→2×→4× ladder independently per side). Fills at or above it are halted. Present only while outside RTH with a sealed anchor; omitted in-RTH and for 24/7 markets.

lowerTradingBound.description: Actual lower price boundary (decimal USD) of the off-hours trading band. Fills at or below it are halted. Present only while outside RTH with a sealed anchor; omitted in-RTH and for 24/7 markets.

nextUpperTradingBound.description: Price (decimal USD) the upper boundary moves to if the upper band expands one level; equals upperTradingBound at the 4× ceiling. Present only while outside RTH with a sealed anchor.

nextLowerTradingBound.description: Price (decimal USD) the lower boundary moves to if the lower band expands one level; equals lowerTradingBound at the 4× ceiling. Present only while outside RTH with a sealed anchor.

isUpperInExpansionZone.description: Whether the upper band side is in its expansion zone — the 1-hour EWMA of the bid-side impact price is holding within 90% of the upper boundary; holding for one continuous hour expands the band one level. The zones are independent per side. Present only while outside RTH with a sealed anchor.

isLowerInExpansionZone.description: Whether the lower band side is in its expansion zone. Present only while outside RTH with a sealed anchor.

upperZoneEnteredAt.description: Unix seconds at which the upper side entered its expansion zone. Present only while isUpperInExpansionZone is true.

upperExpectedExpansionAt.description: Unix seconds of the earliest time the upper bound can expand — exactly one hour after upperZoneEnteredAt. Not a guarantee; the EWMA must still be in the zone when the hour completes. Present only while isUpperInExpansionZone is true.

lowerZoneEnteredAt.description: Unix seconds at which the lower side entered its expansion zone. Present only while isLowerInExpansionZone is true.

lowerExpectedExpansionAt.description: Unix seconds of the earliest time the lower bound can expand. Present only while isLowerInExpansionZone is true.

regularTradingHours.description: Session window during which the base margin fractions apply; outside it the off-hours fractions apply. Omitted for 24/7 markets (crypto).

epoch.description: Batch publish time in Unix nanoseconds.

prices.description: One entry per market updated in this batch.

markPrice.description: Authoritative mark price stamped by the matching engine (decimal string). "0" means unavailable; callers must not fall back to `price`.

markEpochNanos.description: Wall-clock timestamp in Unix nanoseconds at which the mark price was signed. Omitted when unavailable.

bestBid.description: Best bid level, or null when the bid side is empty.

bestAsk.description: Best ask level, or null when the ask side is empty.

timestamp.description: Unix microseconds when the top-of-book was stamped.

lastSequenceId.description: Per-market orderbook sequence for this BBO frame.

marketId.description: Market identifier. BTC-USD is `0` and is always present.

leverage.description: Effective leverage (user override or market default).

isolated.description: `true` = ISOLATED margin mode; `false` = CROSS. Always present. In snapshot frames reflects persisted state; in streaming frames reflects the account's margin mode after the event (defaults to CROSS if the lookup fails).

marginMode.description: Human-readable form of `isolated`. Always present alongside `isolated`.

type.description: Discriminator for account-level fee tier entries.

feeTierLevel.description: Tier level index (0=Base, 1=Bronze, 2=Silver, 3=Gold, 4=Platinum, 5=VIP, 6=Max). Base tier is `0` and is always present.

makerFeePpm.description: Maker fee rate in ppm — parts-per-million of notional (e.g. 200 = 0.02% = 2 bps).

takerFeePpm.description: Taker fee rate in ppm — parts-per-million of notional (e.g. 500 = 0.05% = 5 bps).

AccountAttributesLeverageRejectEntry.description: Emitted (streaming only, never in a snapshot) when the engine REJECTS a setLeverage request. The change did not take effect — `leverage` echoes the account's unchanged current value. Correlate with the originating request via `requestId` (returned in the WS `setLeverage` 202 ACK / the `POST /v1/setLeverage` response). A successful change instead surfaces as an `AccountAttributesLeverageEntry`. When `isolated` was also part of the request the margin mode outcome is folded in via the optional `isolated`, `marginMode`, `marginModeStatus`, and `marginModeRejectReason` fields.

type.description: Discriminator for a rejected setLeverage request.

marketId.description: Market identifier from the rejected request.

marketDisplayName.description: Falls back to `MARKET-<id>` when the market id is unknown (UNKNOWN_MARKET reject).

leverage.description: The account's unchanged current leverage (`0` when no override exists).

status.description: Engine-lifecycle marker. Always `REJECTED` for this entry.

rejectReason.description: Why the engine refused the leverage change.

requestId.description: Correlates with the `requestId` returned in the setLeverage 202 ACK.

isolated.description: Present when `isolated` was supplied on the request. `true` = ISOLATED; `false` = CROSS.

marginMode.description: Human-readable form of `isolated`. Omitted when no margin mode change was requested.

marginModeStatus.description: Outcome of the margin mode portion of the request.

marginModeRejectReason.description: Why the margin mode change was refused. Only present when `marginModeStatus` is `REJECTED`.

isSnapshot.description: True for subscribe-time snapshots; false for streaming deltas.

ExchangeAttributesFeeTierTier.description: One tier row in a feeTierConfig exchange attribute entry.

volumeThreshold.description: 30-day notional volume threshold in USD×1e6 required to reach this tier. Always 0 for the base tier.

makerFeePpm.description: Maker fee rate in ppm — parts-per-million of notional (e.g. 200 = 0.02% = 2 bps). Negative values indicate a maker rebate.

takerFeePpm.description: Taker fee rate in ppm — parts-per-million of notional (e.g. 500 = 0.05% = 5 bps). Always ≥ 0.

ExchangeAttributesEntry.description: A discriminated-union entry in the exchangeAttributeUpdates stream, discriminated by `type`: `"feeTierConfig"` (full fee tier table) or `"marketAttributes"` (per-market RTH / VWAP-seal / trading-bound edge events — DEPRECATED, superseded by the dedicated `marketAttributes` channel whose entries carry the market's full attribute state).

type.description: Discriminator. `"feeTierConfig"` carries the full fee tier table; `"marketAttributes"` carries one per-market RTH or trading-bound event.

tiers.description: Present when `type` is `"feeTierConfig"`. Full replacement of the exchange fee tier table, sorted ascending by level.

isOutsideRth.description: Regular Trading Hours state after the event (marketAttributes entries only).

sealedVwapSettlementPrice.description: Sealed VWAP settlement price (decimal USD) anchoring the off-hours trading band (marketAttributes entries only; omitted when the frame carries no seal).

boundEvent.description: Event kind (marketAttributes entries only; always present on these entries). RTH transitions: `exitRth` (market leaves regular trading hours) / `enterRth` (market re-enters). Off-hours bound events: `expansionZoneEntered` (side's impact-price EWMA crossed within 90% of its trading boundary, starting the 1-hour expansion clock), `expansionZoneExited` (EWMA relaxed out before the hour completed; clock reset), `tradingBoundExpanded` (clock completed; band widened one level on the 0.5×→1×→2×→4× ladder). Every entry also carries the per-side zone state (`upperZoneEnteredAt` / `upperExpectedExpansionAt` / `lowerZoneEnteredAt` / `lowerExpectedExpansionAt`), mirrored on `GET /v1/markets`. (Historical frames may carry the retired `boundHit` / `boundExpand` values.)

boundSide.description: Which band edge fired on bound-event deltas ("upper" / "lower"). Null on RTH-transition (`exitRth` / `enterRth`) and VWAP-seal deltas.

boundPrice.description: Actual boundary price (decimal USD) in force when the bound event fired — the boundary being pressured for a zone event, the pre-expansion boundary for a `tradingBoundExpanded`.

newBoundPrice.description: Boundary price (decimal USD) after the bound event — equals `boundPrice` for zone events, the widened boundary for a `tradingBoundExpanded`.

upperZoneEnteredAt.description: Unix seconds at which the upper side entered its expansion zone, carried on every marketAttributes entry. Omitted when the upper side is not in its zone.

upperExpectedExpansionAt.description: Unix seconds of the earliest time the upper bound can expand (zoneEnteredAt + one hour; not a guarantee — the EWMA must still be in the zone when the hour completes). Omitted when the upper side is not in its zone.

lowerZoneEnteredAt.description: Unix seconds at which the lower side entered its expansion zone. Omitted when the lower side is not in its zone.

lowerExpectedExpansionAt.description: Unix seconds of the earliest time the lower bound can expand. Omitted when the lower side is not in its zone.

timestamp.description: Event time in Unix microseconds (marketAttributes entries only).

marketSequenceNum.description: Per-market transaction sequence number (marketAttributes entries only). One engine transaction can emit several entries for a market (e.g. both bound sides transitioning on one tick) and they share this value — it identifies the transaction, not the individual entry, so do not dedup entries by it alone.

isSnapshot.description: True for the subscribe-time snapshot; false for streaming updates triggered by operator fee tier edits.

MarketAttributesEntry.description: One market's complete RTH / off-hours attribute block. Every attribute field is present on every entry — `null` when it does not currently apply (in-RTH markets carry null bounds; a side not in its expansion zone carries null zone timestamps). Field semantics match the fields of the same names on `GET /v1/markets`. The `boundEvent` / `boundSide` / `timestamp` / `marketSequenceNum` annotations appear only on streaming updates, never on snapshot entries.

offHoursInitialMarginFraction.description: Initial margin fraction the engine enforces outside the market's RTH window (maintenance margin is not uplifted off-hours).

isOutsideRth.description: Current Regular Trading Hours state. Always `false` for 24/7 markets (crypto), which never leave regular trading hours. `null` while the server has not yet learned an RTH market's state (briefly after a deploy).

currentSettlementPrice.description: Sealed VWAP settlement price (decimal USD) anchoring the off-hours trading band. `null` in-RTH (no anchor).

upperTradingBound.description: Actual upper boundary (decimal USD) of the off-hours band: anchor + anchor × initialMarginFraction × bandMultiplier, where the multiplier walks the 0.5×→1×→2×→4× ladder independently per side. `null` in-RTH.

lowerTradingBound.description: Actual lower boundary of the off-hours band. `null` in-RTH.

nextUpperTradingBound.description: Boundary the upper band moves to if it expands one level (equals `upperTradingBound` at the 4× ceiling). `null` in-RTH.

nextLowerTradingBound.description: Boundary the lower band moves to if it expands one level. `null` in-RTH.

isUpperInExpansionZone.description: Whether the upper side is in its expansion zone (its 1-hour impact-price EWMA is holding within 90% of the boundary). `null` in-RTH.

isLowerInExpansionZone.description: Whether the lower side is in its expansion zone. `null` in-RTH.

upperZoneEnteredAt.description: Unix seconds the upper side entered its expansion zone. `null` when not in the zone.

upperExpectedExpansionAt.description:
Earliest Unix seconds the upper bound can expand (zoneEnteredAt
+ one hour; not a guarantee — the EWMA must still be in the zone when the hour completes). `null` when not in the zone.

lowerZoneEnteredAt.description: Unix seconds the lower side entered its expansion zone. `null` when not in the zone.

lowerExpectedExpansionAt.description: Earliest Unix seconds the lower bound can expand. `null` when not in the zone.

boundEvent.description: Event annotation for streaming updates. Omitted only on snapshot entries — always present on delta entries, since every update frame is either an RTH transition or a bound event. `exitRth` (market leaves regular trading hours) / `enterRth` (market re-enters) — the block itself carries the resulting state, so there is no separate bound-price field for these. `expansionZoneEntered` (side's impact-price EWMA crossed within 90% of its boundary, starting the 1-hour expansion clock), `expansionZoneExited` (EWMA relaxed out; clock reset), `tradingBoundExpanded` (clock completed; band widened one level on the 0.5×→1×→2×→4× ladder — the new boundary IS the block's `upperTradingBound` / `lowerTradingBound`).

boundSide.description: Which band edge fired on bound-event deltas ("upper" / "lower"). Null on snapshot entries and on RTH-transition (`exitRth` / `enterRth`) deltas.

timestamp.description: Event time in Unix microseconds (streaming updates only).

marketSequenceNum.description: Per-market transaction sequence number (streaming updates only). Entries emitted by one engine transaction share this value — it identifies the transaction, not the entry, so do not dedup by it alone.

isSnapshot.description: True for the subscribe-time snapshot (one entry per RTH market); false for streaming updates (one entry for the affected market).

marketId.description: Perpetual market identifier (uint16). Map to display name via `GET /markets`.

price.description: Limit price. All TPSL lifecycle events (TPSL_PLACED, TPSL_TRIGGERED, TPSL_CANCELED, trigger-time REJECTED) carry the leg's limit price here; market-type TPSLs placed without a price report "0" — use triggerPrice for the trigger level.

avgFillPrice.description: Cumulative average fill price across all fills of this order. Present whenever the order has any filled quantity; absent when nothing has filled. Matches the REST / snapshot `avgFillPrice`.

triggerPrice.description: Set for TP/SL orders only — on TP/SL events and on a REJECTED event for a TP/SL order rejected at placement or at trigger time (e.g. a triggered reduce-only TP/SL whose position flipped, or a triggered FOK that cannot fully fill). A TP/SL that converted to a regular order and was rejected after conversion does not carry TP/SL fields.

cancelReason.description: Qualifies a CANCELED update when the matching engine stamped a reason. Currently the only value is MODIFY_CANCELED: this cancel is the first leg of a modify — the SAME orderId is re-placed by the account's very next update (PLACED / FILLED / REJECTED), so the order is not terminally gone unless that follow-up says so. Absent on all other cancels, which are genuinely terminal.

state.description: Order lifecycle state after this event. `PARTIALLY_FILLED` is terminal for IOC orders. Any explicit cancel produces `CANCELED` even when prior fills had already partially filled the order.

positionEffect.description: How this fill changed the account's position. Only set on fill events; absent on placements/cancels/rejects. `FLIP_*` covers a position that closed and reopened on the opposite side within one user order.

createdAt.description: Order placement time (epoch microseconds); stable across updates.

updatedAt.description: Time of this update event (epoch microseconds).

sequenceNumber.description: Per-account sequence of this order event (same counter as AccountUpdate.sequenceNumber).

FundingPayment.description: One applied funding payment for an (account, market) at a single funding payment time. Same shape as REST `GET /v1/funding` `FundingPayment`.

size.description: Signed position size when the payment was computed.

payment.description: Quote-currency amount applied. Positive = trader received, negative = trader paid.

fundingPayments.description: Up to 100 most recent funding payments.

PredictedFundingRate.description: Predicted next-hour funding rate as published by the funder. Not wrapped in an isSnapshot envelope. May be empty in the subscribe-time snapshot when no prediction is cached for the market yet.

rate1h.description: Predicted 1-hour funding rate as a decimal string.

AccountTransferEvent.description: One account transfer event. Same shape as `AccountTransferEvent` in `openapi.yaml`.

amount.description: Credited (deposit / transfer-in) or debited (withdrawal / transfer-out) amount as a decimal string.

netQuoteBalance.description: Perspective account's post-event aggregate cash balance as a decimal string.

globalSequenceId.description: Strict ordering across all engine events.

accountSequenceNum.description: Post-op per-account sequence number for the perspective account. Matches `AccountUpdate.sequenceNum`.

sourceAccountId.description: Sender's wire account ID. Populated only for transfer events.

destinationAccountId.description: Recipient's wire account ID. Populated only for transfer events.

isSnapshot.description: True for the subscribe-time snapshot; false for streaming updates.

accountTransferEvents.description: Newest-first in snapshots; exactly one event in streaming updates.

candles.description: Oldest first. Last entry is the open (in-progress) bar.

openTime.description: Unix timestamp (microseconds) of the bar open (candle bucket start).

isFinal.description: True when the bar is closed and will not be updated again.

SignedRequest.description: Signing fields required for all order mutation requests.

timestamp.description: Unix epoch nanoseconds as a string. Millisecond or second epochs are rejected with `401`; must be within ±30s of server wall-clock.

signature.description: Ed25519 signature (128 hex characters). For `placeOrder`, `cancelOrder`, and `modifyOrder` sign the **typed canonical payload** (the JSON object IS the signing message).             For legacy methods (`cancelAllOrders`, `setLeverage`, `adjustIsolatedMargin`) sign `timestamp + action + canonicalJSON(request.payload)` where `action` is the canonical camelCase method name.

BatchSignedRequest.description: Envelope signing fields for BATCH order mutations (batchPlaceOrders / batchCancelOrders). Unlike `SignedRequest`, there is NO envelope `signature` — each element of the batch array carries its own per-order `signature` instead. Only the shared `apiKey` + `timestamp` live here.

timestamp.description: Unix epoch nanoseconds as a string, shared by every order in the batch. Millisecond or second epochs are rejected with `401`; must be within ±30s of server wall-clock.

OrderRequestItem.description: A single order. Identical shape to the `placeOrder` payload and to each element of a `batchPlaceOrders` `orders` array.

address.description: Master EVM address; must match the API key's master account.

orderType.description: Execution style. TPSL trigger orders are still `LIMIT` or `MARKET` here — the trigger semantics come from `tpslType` + `stopPrice`.

timeInForce.description: GTT = Good Till Time (rests until goodTilTime), IOC = Immediate or Cancel, FOK = Fill or Kill, ALO = Add Liquidity Only (post-only). Note: order reads currently report resting orders as GTC (legacy name for GTT). Reduce-only non-TPSL orders must be IOC or FOK. TPSL LIMIT legs must be GTT.

goodTilTime.description: Order expiry as an epoch-microsecond timestamp (string). REQUIRED for all order types, including IOC/FOK (which never rest) — a mandatory replay-protection timestamp; omitting it is rejected with `goodTilTime is required`. Must be at least one month in the future. Covered by the per-order signature (`g`, in nanoseconds).

quantity.description: Order size in base asset, human-readable decimal. Must be at most the market's `maxOrderSize` (see `GET /markets`); reduce-only orders are **not** exempt — rejected with `OrderSizeTooLarge`.

price.description: Human-readable decimal price. Required for `LIMIT` orders (resting limit price) and for **all** `MARKET` orders (protective slippage bound). For plain `MARKET` orders the value must be a positive decimal within **10% of the current mark price**; orders outside this band are rejected with `MarketPriceSlippageToleranceTooHigh`. For TPSL `MARKET` orders the value must be within **10% of `stopPrice`** (trigger price) — at trigger time the mark price ≈ stopPrice, so this enforces the same ±10% slippage protection.

clientTime.description: Optional client timestamp (Unix nanoseconds, as a string) — the signed `ct`; when set it must equal the envelope `timestamp`.

reduceOnly.description: If true, the order can only reduce an existing position.

minSize.description: Optional minimum fill size, human-readable decimal.

stopPrice.description: Trigger price for TPSL orders, human-readable decimal. Required when `tpslType` is set.

tpslType.description: Marks the order as a take-profit / stop-loss trigger order. Omit for plain orders. For `LIMIT` execution, `timeInForce` must be `GTT`.

signature.description: Per-order Ed25519 signature (128 hex), REQUIRED when this order is an element of a `batchPlaceOrders` array, omitted for single `placeOrder`. Signed over the typed canonical `placeOrder` payload (op=1; op=4 for TPSL legs) — identical to the bytes signed for a standalone `placeOrder`. The shared `timestamp` envelope value is the `ct` field inside the payload.

CancelRequestItem.description: A single cancel. Identical shape to the `cancelOrder` payload and to each element of a `batchCancelOrders` `cancels` array. Provide exactly one of `orderId` or `clientId` (use `kind` to disambiguate when both could apply).

address.description: Master EVM address; must match the API key's master account.

kind.description: Which identifier to cancel by. Defaults to `orderId` when `orderId` is present.

orderId.description: System order id. One of `orderId` or `clientId` is required.

clientId.description: Client-supplied order id from the prior `placeOrder`.

validUntil.description: Optional expiry for the cancel itself (unix seconds).

signature.description: Per-cancel Ed25519 signature (128 hex), REQUIRED when this cancel is an element of a `batchCancelOrders` array, omitted for single `cancelOrder`. Signed over the typed canonical `cancelOrder` payload — identical to the bytes signed for a standalone `cancelOrder`. The shared `timestamp` envelope value is the `ct` field inside the payload.

ModifyRequestItem.description: A single modify. Identical shape to the `modifyOrder` payload and to each element of a `batchModifyOrders` `modifies` array. Identify the order to modify by **exactly one** of `orderId` or `clientId` — providing both (or neither) is rejected.

address.description: Master EVM address; must match the API key's master account.

orderId.description: Server order id to modify. Provide exactly one of `orderId` or `clientId`.

clientId.description: Placement-time client id identifying the order to modify (resolved engine-side against the account's client-id index). Provide exactly one of `orderId` or `clientId` — supplying both is rejected. Lets a client modify an order before the place response (with the server orderId) has arrived.

quantity.description: New size, human-readable decimal. Must be at most the market's `maxOrderSize`; reduce-only orders are not exempt — rejected with `OrderSizeTooLarge`.

timeInForce.description: GTT = Good Till Time (rests until goodTilTime), IOC = Immediate or Cancel, FOK = Fill or Kill, ALO = Add Liquidity Only (post-only). Note: order reads currently report resting orders as GTC (legacy name for GTT).

reduceOnly.description: Reduce-only flag. Required — must be explicitly true or false (immutable; echo the resting order's value). Covered by the request signature.

goodTilTime.description: Required — the order's expiry as epoch microseconds (string), echoed from placement (a differing value performs a cancel-replace with the new expiry). Must be at least one month in the future. Covered by the request signature (`g`, in nanoseconds).

clientTime.description: Optional client timestamp (Unix nanoseconds, as a string) — the signed `ct`; when set it must equal the envelope `timestamp`.

signature.description: Per-modify Ed25519 signature (128 hex), REQUIRED when this modify is an element of a `batchModifyOrders` array, omitted for single `modifyOrder`. Signed over the typed canonical `modifyOrder` payload — identical to the bytes signed for a standalone `modifyOrder`. The shared `timestamp` envelope value is the `ct` field inside the payload.

id.description: Client-chosen request id, echoed in the response.

address.description: Master EVM address; must match the API key's master account.

marketId.description: Optional market scope. Omit to cancel every open order across all markets on the account.

validUntil.description: Optional expiry for the cancel-all itself (unix seconds).

marketId.description: Optional market scope. Omit for an account-wide switch; set to scope the switch to a single market. Independent of the account-wide switch and of other per-market switches on the same subaccount, and selects which switch to arm/refresh/disarm.

time.description: Absolute epoch microseconds deadline; omit or null to disarm. Each refresh must send a new later deadline (5s–5min ahead of now).

orders.description: Orders to place. All must share the same `address` / `accountIndex`; the server resolves identity from the first entry and overrides `address` on the rest.

grouping.description: Selects the wire message family. Defaults to `na` (plain orders). Any TPSL grouping requires every order to set `tpslType` + `stopPrice` (except the single entry order in an `entryTpsl` bundle).

cancels.description: Cancels to submit. All must share the same `address` / `accountIndex`; the server resolves identity from the first entry.

modifies.description: Modifies to submit. All must share the same `address` / `accountIndex`; the server resolves identity from the first entry. Failures are per element.

leverage.description: Leverage to set. Must be in `[1, market max]`.

isolated.description: Optional. When present, also sets the margin mode: `true` for isolated, `false` for cross. Omit to leave the current margin mode unchanged.

accountIndex.description: Subaccount index (0–9). Required in the signed payload; omit or send `0` for the primary account.

amount.description: Dollar amount to move, as a decimal string (e.g. `"100"` for $100). Do not send quote quantums — the gateway converts dollars to quantums (1e9 = $1) for the engine. Positive moves cross → isolated (adds margin to the leg); negative moves isolated → cross (removes margin from the leg). Zero is rejected with HTTP 400.

id.description: Client-chosen request id, echoed in the response.

payload.description:
Method-specific parameters. `market` required for market-scoped RPCs.

An optional `market` filter is accepted by every market-scoped read: `fills`, `orders`, `positions`, `leverages`, `mids`, and `prices`. It takes either the display ticker (`BTC-USD`, case-insensitive) or the numeric market id (`1`), resolved by the same code as the REST `?market=` query param. Omit it to get every market; an unresolvable value returns 400 rather than a silent all-markets response. On `mids` and `prices` a filter naming an OFFLINE market returns an empty object, matching how the unfiltered response omits offline markets.

Account-scoped list RPCs take the same filters as their REST equivalents: `orders` accepts `market` and `status`, `fills` accepts `market` and `role`. On `orders`, both filters apply to the `openOrders` and `recentClosedOrders` halves of the result, and `status` accepts either a JSON array (`["OPEN","CANCELED"]`) or a comma-separated string (`"OPEN,CANCELED"`) — the same two spellings as the REST `?status=` param. Values are `OPEN`, `UNTRIGGERED`, `FILLED`, `CANCELED`, `REJECTED`, `LIQUIDATED`, `ADL`, case-insensitive; an unrecognised value returns 400. `status` matches each order's current status, not any status it held earlier in its life.

status.description: HTTP-like status. 200 = success with a definitive engine ack, 202 = accepted (not terminal — observe `orders`/`userFills` for the lifecycle), 4xx = client error, 5xx = gateway error.

field.description: Field that caused the error, if applicable.

retryAfterMs.description: Present only on 429 (rate-limit) errors. Precise milliseconds the client should wait before retrying. Mirrors the REST 429 body's `retryAfterMs` field.
